title: Regular schemes are normal; the normal decomposition
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Call $X$ normal if every local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], that is, an integral domain integrally closed in its field of fractions.

(1) If $X$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme], then $X$ is normal.

(2) If $X$ is Noetherian (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact, meaning every open covering has a finite subcover) and normal, then $X$ is a finite disjoint union of normal integral schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme]. More precisely, its irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] are pairwise disjoint open and closed subsets, and with their open subscheme structures they are normal and integral.

(3) In particular, if $X$ is regular, Noetherian, nonempty and connected (its underlying space is not the union of two disjoint nonempty open subsets), then $X$ is irreducible. Nonemptiness is explicit because irreducibility includes nonemptiness, whereas connectedness alone here allows the empty space.

proof.text: Assume $X$ is regular. By [def-weil-regular-scheme], choose an affine open cover $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ with every $R_i$ a regular ring. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal], every $R_i$ is normal. For $x\in U_i$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with $(R_i)_{\mathfrak p_x}$. By [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], this localization is a normal domain. Every point is in some $U_i$, so $X$ is normal. This also covers the empty scheme, with the empty cover.

source.place: Tag 0569, label lemma-regular-normal; Tag 02IT, label lemma-characterize-regular (use the affine-cover definition)

proof.text: For (2), assume $X$ is Noetherian and normal. Each stalk is a domain, so its only nilpotent is zero: $a^n=0$ in a domain implies $a=0$ by repeated use of the absence of zero divisors. Thus $X$ is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme], and that node also states that every ring of sections is reduced. Choose an affine open cover $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ with each $R_i$ Noetherian, using local Noetherianity as defined in [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Each $R_i$ is reduced by the preceding observation.

source.place: Tag 033I, label definition-normal; Tag 033K, label lemma-normal-reduced; Tag 0357, label lemma-normal-locally-finite-nr-irreducibles, affine case

proof.text: For every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R_i$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points] gives its corresponding point $x\in U_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $(R_i)_{\mathfrak p}\cong\mathcal O_{X,x}$, a normal domain. Hence $R_i$ is a normal ring by [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Since $R_i$ is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes] gives finitely many minimal primes. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-normal-iff-integrally-closed-total-fractions] to the reduced ring $R_i$ from step 2: it is isomorphic to a finite product $\prod_j A_{ij}$ of normal domains. All three required hypotheses, reducedness, finiteness of minimal primes, and normality, have now been verified.

source.place: Tag 0357, label lemma-normal-locally-finite-nr-irreducibles, affine case; Algebra Tag 030C, label lemma-characterize-reduced-ring-normal

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum], $U_i\cong\coprod_j\operatorname{Spec}A_{ij}$, with each factor an open and closed subscheme; the disjoint-open description is [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Each factor is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field], since $A_{ij}$ is a domain. It is normal: its stalk at $\mathfrak q$ is $(A_{ij})_{\mathfrak q}$ by that same node, and is a normal domain by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain]. In particular the factors are nonempty and irreducible by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. They are exactly the irreducible components of $U_i$: an irreducible subset cannot meet two disjoint clopen factors, and each irreducible factor is already maximal among irreducible subsets. The empty product presents the empty affine open and creates no component.

source.place: Tag 0357, label lemma-normal-locally-finite-nr-irreducibles, affine case; Algebra Tag 030C

proof.text: Let $T$ be an irreducible component of $X$. For every $U_i$ meeting $T$, [lem-sc-components-open-injection] says that $T\cap U_i$ is an irreducible component of $U_i$. Step 4 identifies it with a clopen normal integral factor of $U_i$; thus $T\cap U_i$ is open in $X$. Their union is $T$, so $T$ is open, and it is closed by [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Distinct components $T,T'$ are disjoint: if $x\in T\cap T'$, take $U_i\ni x$. Their intersections with $U_i$ are components of the disjoint decomposition in step 4 and meet at $x$, so they coincide. The injectivity assertion of [lem-sc-components-open-injection] then gives $T=T'$, a contradiction.

The components cover $X$ by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], and there are finitely many by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components], because $X$ is Noetherian. Equip each component $T$ with its open subscheme structure. Its stalks are those of $X$ at the same points, by the restriction description in [def-weil-open-immersion]; hence it is normal and reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. It is nonempty and irreducible as a component, so it is integral by the equivalence in [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The canonical morphism from the scheme coproduct in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] to $X$ is an isomorphism: on each disjoint open component it is the identity of that open subscheme, and these local inverses agree on the empty intersections and glue by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. The two composites are the identity on each covering open, hence are identities by the uniqueness assertion of that node. This proves the finite disjoint-union assertion, also for $X=\varnothing$, where the index set is empty.

source.place: Tag 033M, label lemma-normal-Noetherian, using Tag 0357, label lemma-normal-locally-finite-nr-irreducibles

proof.text: For (3), a regular $X$ is normal by step 1, and step 6 applies because $X$ is Noetherian. Nonemptiness ensures there is a component. If there were another, one component and the union of all the others would be disjoint nonempty open subsets covering $X$, contrary to connectedness. Thus there is exactly one component and it is all of $X$. It is irreducible by [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Without nonemptiness the decomposition can have zero components, so this last inference would fail.

lean.statement: theorem regular_normal_and_normal_decomposition (X : Scheme.{u}) : ((∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.affineOpens, x ∈ (U : X.Opens) ∧ IsRegularRing Γ(X, U)) → ∀ x : X, IsDomain (X.presheaf.stalk x) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (X.presheaf.stalk x)) ∧ (IsNoetherian X → (∀ x : X, IsDomain (X.presheaf.stalk x) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (X.presheaf.stalk x)) → ∃ (n : ℕ) (U : Fin n → X.Opens), Set.range (fun i : Fin n ↦ (U i : Set X)) = irreducibleComponents X ∧ (∀ i : Fin n, IsClosed (U i : Set X)) ∧ (∀ i j : Fin n, i ≠ j → Disjoint (U i) (U j)) ∧ (⨆ i : Fin n, U i) = ⊤ ∧ (∀ i : Fin n, IsIntegral (U i).toScheme ∧ ∀ x : (U i).toScheme, IsDomain ((U i).toScheme.presheaf.stalk x) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed ((U i).toScheme.presheaf.stalk x)) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk X (fun i : Fin n ↦ (U i).ι)))) ∧ ((∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.affineOpens, x ∈ (U : X.Opens) ∧ IsRegularRing Γ(X, U)) → IsNoetherian X → Nonempty X → PreconnectedSpace X → IrreducibleSpace X)
